advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip the upper-bound guard when metered.saw_datapoints is False, matching the empty-read handling the enforcement path already relies on.
evidence: handler.py:405 `if metered is None or metered.degraded:` — no check of `metered.saw_datapoints`
handler.py:411 `if metered.total >= actual:` then falls through to `_notify("Bedrock cap upper-bound invariant VIOLATED" ...)`

_metered_spend contract handler.py:161-164 `# False when every query returned no datapoints. Zero tokens and "the metric pipeline told us nothing" are the same number but not the same fact, and the release decision turns on which one it is.`
The guard cannot distinguish 'checked, estimate genuinely below actual' from 'the metered instrument returned nothing for the settled day' — the check fails toward a false positive alert.
handler.py:401-403 `except ClientError as exc: log.warning(...); return` — `state["guard_day"]` is only set at line 404 AFTER the try block
README/commit: 'It costs one extra Cost Explorer request per day'
advisory.finding: The upper-bound guard treats an empty CloudWatch read as a real invariant violation: it skips only when the metered signal is None or degraded, but not when metered.saw_datapoints is False, so a settled-day read that succeeds with zero datapoints (transient metric-delivery gap, aged-out data, or a quiet region) yields metered.total==0 and fires a spurious 'invariant VIOLATED' alert whenever actual exceeds the noise floor.
merged_from: On the CE ClientError branch the guard returns without setting state['guard_day'], so the extra Cost Explorer read is retried on every 5-minute tick until it succeeds, contradicting the 'one extra Cost Explorer request per day' claim in the commit message and README during any CE outage.
scenarios: A CloudWatch metric-delivery gap or region hiccup for the 2-days-ago window returns no datapoints while CE billed a normal (>5% of cap) day
Metric data for the settled hourly period is unavailable/aged in one region
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the guard skip to `if metered is None or metered.degraded or not metered.saw_datapoints:` so an all-empty settled-day read is treated as 'signal incomplete' rather than a violation.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Record guard_day (or otherwise throttle the guard's CE call) even when _ce_spend_today raises, so a persistent CE failure cannot issue an extra CE request on every 5-minute tick.
evidence: handler.py:395 `if state.get("guard_day") == day.isoformat(): return`
handler.py:397-402 `try: actual = _ce_spend_today(day) ... except ClientError as exc: log.warning(...); return` — returns before `state["guard_day"] = day.isoformat()` on line 403
commit message: 'It costs one extra Cost Explorer request per day'
The guard call at handler.py:564 is unconditional and outside the CE_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS poll gate
advisory.finding: The daily upper-bound guard issues a Cost Explorer GetCostAndUsage request on every 5-minute invocation until it succeeds, because _guard_upper_bound_invariant calls _ce_spend_today before recording guard_day and returns without setting guard_day when the CE call raises ClientError. On a persistent CE outage this makes one extra CE request per tick for the whole day, not the documented 'one extra Cost Explorer request per day', adding unbounded CE request cost.
scenarios: Cost Explorer is throttling or erroring for a sustained window while the Lambda continues its 5-minute schedule

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a guard test where _ce_spend_today raises ClientError and assert no SNS publish, no state['guard_day'] set, and the handler still completes.
evidence: handler.py:397-403: `try: actual = _ce_spend_today(day) ... except ClientError as exc: log.warning("upper-bound guard could not read its signals: %s", exc); return`
All guard tests build a clean FakeCE without error: `ce=FakeCE(spend=THRESHOLD)` / `FakeCE(spend=tiny)` (lines 1464,1477,1488,1498,1511); none pass `error=client_error(...)`

Named violating input: `_ce_spend_today` raising `ClientError("GetCostAndUsage")` for the settled day — a regression that set state['guard_day'] before the try (poisoning the retry) or that let the exception escape and abort the handler would pass every existing guard test.
handler.py:405-407: `if metered is None or metered.degraded: log.info(...); return`

_guard_module always builds a non-degraded signal: `module._metered_spend = lambda day_start, now: module.MeteredSpend(total=metered_total, degraded=False, failures=(), saw_datapoints=True)` (lines 1455-1457)

Named violating input: a degraded MeteredSpend with total below `actual` (e.g. degraded_metered_spend(module, 1) with FakeCE(spend=THRESHOLD)) — dropping the `metered.degraded` check would fire a false VIOLATED notification from a partial reading, undetected by any test.
advisory.finding: The guard's ClientError skip branch is never exercised: no test makes _ce_spend_today or _metered_spend raise a ClientError inside _guard_upper_bound_invariant, so the log-and-return-without-notifying, without-setting-guard_day behavior added at handler.py:401-403 is unverified.
merged_from: The guard's degraded/None metered-signal skip branch (handler.py:405) is untested: every guard test uses a clean MeteredSpend(degraded=False), so the requirement that an incomplete metered reading skips silently rather than raising a spurious upper-bound-VIOLATED warning is unverified.
scenarios: Cost Explorer or CloudWatch transiently errors during the daily guard read
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test passing ce=FakeCE(error=client_error("GetCostAndUsage")) to _guard_module and assert fake_aws.sns.published == [] and 'guard_day' not in state.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the always-true `assert ... else True` line in test_guard_never_touches_iam or replace it with a concrete no-attach assertion.
evidence: assert fake_aws.iam.attached == [] if hasattr(fake_aws.iam, "attached") else True
FakeIAM defines no `attached` attribute (class body lines 152-188 exposes role_policies/group_policies only), so hasattr is always False and the assertion is `assert True`.
advisory.finding: test_guard_never_touches_iam ends with a no-op assertion that always evaluates True, giving a false impression of an extra check: FakeIAM has no `attached` attribute, so `hasattr(...)` is False and the ternary reduces to `assert True`.
advisory.suggested_fix: Delete line 1507; the role_policies/group_policies equality assertions already establish the contract.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Relax the affirmative-prose README/docstring assertions to structural markers (e.g. section headings) or drop the exact-sentence matches.
evidence: assert "upper bound on real spend, not an estimate of it" in readme
assert "trip the cap well below the configured dollar figure" in readme
These tokens are prose read only by a human/LLM; no parser, validator, or CI runner branches on their exact value, so per the Rule-5 litmus they are wording guards, not structural-boundary contracts.
advisory.finding: test_readme_states_the_upper_bound_and_its_cost and test_module_docstring_no_longer_describes_a_derived_rate_table assert exact prose phrases from the README/docstring, making them change-detectors on author wording rather than on any machine-consumed contract.
scenarios: A benign reword of the README/docstring that preserves meaning
